blocks.text: A report, a blog, a term paper or a book chapter – AI helps you from the plan to the last edit. But you stay the author.

items: Plan: ask for a structure (sections, main points).
Draft: write part by part, not everything at once.
Edit: ask it to shorten, clarify or change the tone.

blocks.text: I'm writing a 2-page report for my director about the results of a project [project description]. Suggest a structure with headings and what each part should contain. Don't write the full text yet.
Paste an example of your own writing and say: "Write in this style." That way the text sounds like you, not like a robot.
Don't hand in AI-written text as your own if your school or work rules don't allow it. And always check facts and quotes.
Claude is especially good with longer texts and can write in your style if you give it an example.
ChatGPT has a special editing view (Canvas) where you can change the text part by part.
Gemini can also help you directly in Google Docs, on some plans.
